revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Sealed Vault
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Ortiz found a 7/8-yard length of security cable at the crime scene. Forensics needs to cut it into 1/16-yard pieces to test each segment for fingerprints. How many 1/16-yard pieces can she cut from the cable? Show your division equation and explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Ortiz needs to find how many 1/16-yard pieces fit into the 7/8-yard cable, so the dividend is 7/8 and the divisor is 1/16: 7/8 ÷ 1/16. Keep 7/8, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/16 to its reciprocal 16/1: 7/8 × 16/1 = 112/8 = 14. The quotient 14 is already simplified, so Ortiz can cut 14 pieces of security cable, each 1/16 yard long.

vocabulary.definition: Finding how many groups of one fraction fit inside another amount.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar cuántos grupos de una fracción caben dentro de otra cantidad.
vocabulary.visual: 3 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 3; the answer is 6.

vocabulary.definition: The number you are splitting up in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que estás repartiendo en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, the dividend is 3 — it is the total being split
vocabulary.cloze: In 6 ÷ 1/2, the number 6 being divided is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: Find how many fractional groups fit in a whole number by multiplying by the reciprocal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar cuántos grupos fraccionarios caben en un número entero multiplicando por el recíproco.

vocabulary.definition: A counting number with no fraction or decimal, like 0, 1, 2, 3.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número de contar sin fracción ni decimal, como 0, 1, 2, 3.
vocabulary.visual: 4 is a whole number; as a fraction it is 4/1
vocabulary.cloze: A counting number like 0, 1, 2, or 3 with no fraction or decimal part is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar la primera fracción por el recíproco de la segunda fracción.

vocabulary.definition: The number you split by in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número entre el que divides en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, the divisor is 1/4 — it is the size of each piece
vocabulary.cloze: In 6 ÷ 1/2, the number 1/2 we divide by is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que muestra una parte de un todo, como 3/4.
vocabulary.visual: 1/2 means 1 out of 2 equal parts — like cutting a sandwich in half and taking one piece
vocabulary.cloze: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4, is a ___.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 2.1–2.3: 2.1 Interpret Division of Fractions, 2.2 Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions, 2.3 Divide Fractions. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 2.1–2.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 2.1: Dividing by a fraction smaller than 1 gives an answer BIGGER than what you started with, because many tiny pieces fit inside. • 2.2: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal (the fraction flipped over). • 2.3: To divide fractions, multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second, then simplify the answer.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 2.1 — Interpret Division of Fractions: Dividing by a fraction smaller than 1 gives an answer BIGGER than what you started with, because many tiny pieces fit inside.
Lesson 2.2 — Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal (the fraction flipped over).
Lesson 2.3 — Divide Fractions: To divide fractions, multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second, then simplify the answer.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 2.1: Let's try 2 ÷ 1/3. How many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2?
From 2.2: Let's try 3 ÷ 1/4 together. What do we keep? The 3.
From 2.3: Let's try 1/2 ÷ 1/4. Keep 1/2, change to ×, flip 1/4 to 4/1.

youDo.title: Show you're caught up

Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.instructions: Use the bar model to see how many 1/12-pound portions fit into 5/6 pound.
explore.label: How many 1/12s fit into 5/6?
explore.questionText: How many 1/12-pound portions fit into 5/6 pound?

discourse.prompt: Why does 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10? How does the bar model show this?
discourse.sentenceFrame: 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10 because 5/6 is the same as ___ twelfths, and ___ twelfths divided by 1 twelfth = ___.

optional.stem: (Lesson 2.1) Agent Cole has 8 feet of evidence rope and cuts it into 1/3-foot pieces for tagging. What does 8 ÷ 1/3 mean?
choices: How many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 8 feet
8 feet shortened by 1/3 of a foot
8 pieces that are each 1/3 foot long
optional.explanation: Dividing by 1/3 asks how many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 8 feet. Each foot holds 3 thirds, so 8 × 3 = 24 pieces.
choiceFeedback: You're thinking of multiplication. Does dividing by 1/3 ask 'how many parts' or 'what is part of the whole'?
Subtracting doesn't match the problem. Division by fractions asks 'how many pieces fit.'
That's describing the pieces, not what 8 ÷ 1/3 means. What question does the division ask?
optional.stemEs: El agente Cole tiene 8 pies de cuerda de evidencia y la corta en piezas de 1/3 de pie para etiquetarlas. ¿Qué significa 8 ÷ 1/3?
optional.explanationEs: Dividir entre 1/3 pregunta cuántas piezas de 1/3 de pie caben en 8 pies. Cada pie contiene 3 tercios, así que 8 × 3 = 24 piezas.
hints: Dividing by a fraction always asks the same question: how many pieces of that size fit inside the whole amount?
Name the two parts of the problem first — the whole amount of rope and the length of one piece. The whole amount comes first in the division.
Here the whole amount is 8 feet and each piece is 1/3 foot. Picture a single foot of rope: how many 1/3-foot pieces does one foot hold? Then extend that thinking to all 8 feet.
hintsEs: Dividir entre una fracción siempre hace la misma pregunta: ¿cuántas piezas de ese tamaño caben dentro de la cantidad total?
Primero nombra las dos partes del problema: la cantidad total de cuerda y el largo de una pieza. La cantidad total va primero en la división.
Aquí la cantidad total es 8 pies y cada pieza mide 1/3 de pie. Imagina un solo pie de cuerda: ¿cuántas piezas de 1/3 de pie caben en un pie? Luego extiende esa idea a los 8 pies.
choicesEs: Cuántas piezas de 1/3 de pie caben en 8 pies
8 piezas que miden 1/3 de pie cada una

optional.stem: (Lesson 2.2) Detective Park has 4 cups of flour. Each batch of evidence-cookies needs 1/2 cup. How many batches can he make?
optional.explanation: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2/1 = 8 batches. Each cup makes 2 half-cup batches.
choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?
Division by a fraction asks 'how many fit,' not multiplication.
That's computing division by whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/3 is different.
optional.stemEs: El detective Park tiene 4 tazas de harina. Cada tanda de galletas de evidencia necesita 1/2 taza. ¿Cuántas tandas puede hacer?
optional.explanationEs: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2/1 = 8 tandas. Cada taza alcanza para 2 tandas de media taza.
hints: Dividing by a fraction asks how many of those pieces fit inside the total, here how many half cups fit in 4 cups.
Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip the fraction to its reciprocal.
4 ÷ 1/2 becomes 4 × 2/1. Finish that multiplication to count the batches.
hintsEs: Dividir entre una fracción pregunta cuántas de esas piezas caben en el total; aquí, cuántas medias tazas caben en 4 tazas.
Mantén el primer número, cambia ÷ por × e invierte la fracción a su recíproco.
4 ÷ 1/2 se convierte en 4 × 2/1. Termina esa multiplicación para contar las tandas.

choiceFeedback: That's computing with whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/4 is different than dividing by 4.
You need to divide by the fraction, not by its denominator alone.
Does dividing by a fraction smaller than 1 make the answer bigger or smaller?
hints: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal — the same fraction turned upside down.
Keep 3/4 as it is, flip 1/2 to 2/1, and change the ÷ sign into ×.
That gives (3/4) × (2/1). Multiply the numerators and the denominators, then simplify what you get.
hintsEs: Dividir entre una fracción significa multiplicar por su recíproco, es decir, la misma fracción puesta de cabeza.
Deja 3/4 tal como está, invierte 1/2 para obtener 2/1 y cambia el signo ÷ por ×.
Eso da (3/4) × (2/1). Multiplica los numeradores y los denominadores, y luego simplifica lo que obtengas.

approaching.explanation: 3 ÷ 1/4 asks: how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 3? The answer is 12, because each whole has 4 fourths, and 3 × 4 = 12.
choiceFeedback: That's multiplication (3 × 1/4). Division asks 'how many' pieces, not 'groups of' pieces.
Subtraction is not division. Division by a fraction asks 'how many pieces fit.'
That's finding a part of the whole. Division by a fraction asks 'how many of this size fit inside.'
hints: Re-read the expression: 3 is the total amount and 1/4 is the size of one piece. What question could that setup be asking?
Dividing by a fraction asks a counting question about pieces, not 'a part of.' Predict: should the result be bigger or smaller than 3?
Picture a 3-foot tape cut into 1/4-foot pieces. One whole foot already holds 4 of them — what question are you answering as you count?
approaching.explanationEs: 3 ÷ 1/4 pregunta: ¿cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/4 caben en 3? La respuesta es 12, porque cada entero tiene 4 cuartos, y 3 × 4 = 12.
choicesEs: Cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/4 caben en 3
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la expresión: 3 es la cantidad total y 1/4 es el tamaño de una pieza. ¿Qué pregunta podría estar haciendo ese planteamiento?
Dividir entre una fracción hace una pregunta de conteo sobre piezas, no de 'una parte de'. Predice: ¿el resultado debe ser mayor o menor que 3?
Imagina una cinta de 3 pies cortada en piezas de 1/4 de pie. Un pie entero ya tiene 4 de ellas: ¿qué pregunta respondes al contarlas?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 2.1) Which expression means 'how many 1/3-size pieces are in 2'?
approaching.explanation: Finding how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2 is represented by 2 ÷ 1/3. The answer is 6.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies instead of divides. To find how many pieces fit, we divide by the piece size.
You flipped the order. The whole (2) goes first; the piece size (1/3) is the divisor.
Addition combines amounts. To find how many pieces fit, we divide.
hints: Find the two jobs: which number is the total being split, and which is the size of each piece?
Division setups read total ÷ piece size. The total always sits in front of the ÷ sign.
Here the total is 2 and each piece is 1/3. Build the expression with the total first, then check it against each choice.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué expresión significa "cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/3 hay en 2"?
approaching.explanationEs: Encontrar cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/3 caben en 2 se representa con 2 ÷ 1/3. La respuesta es 6.
hintsEs: Encuentra los dos papeles: ¿cuál número es el total que se reparte y cuál es el tamaño de cada pieza?
Los planteamientos de división se leen total ÷ tamaño de la pieza. El total siempre va delante del signo ÷.
Aquí el total es 2 y cada pieza es 1/3. Arma la expresión con el total primero y luego compárala con cada opción.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?
Division by a fraction asks 'how many fit,' not multiplication.
That's computing division by whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/3 is different.
hints: 6 ÷ 1/3 asks how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 6 wholes. Predict: bigger or smaller than 6?
Use Keep, Change, Flip: keep the 6, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/3.
The flip turns 1/3 into 3/1. Set up 6 × 3 and finish the multiplication.
hintsEs: 6 ÷ 1/3 pregunta cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/3 caben en 6 enteros. Predice: ¿mayor o menor que 6?
Usa Conserva, Cambia, Invierte: conserva el 6, cambia ÷ por × e invierte el divisor 1/3.
Al invertir, 1/3 se vuelve 3/1. Plantea 6 × 3 y termina la multiplicación.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?
Division by a fraction asks 'how many fit,' not multiplication.
That's computing division by whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/3 is different.
hints: The total is 3 wholes and each piece is 1/5 — every whole holds several fifths.
Keep, Change, Flip: keep 3, change ÷ to ×, and flip 1/5 upside down.
1/5 flips to 5/1. Multiply 3 by 5 to count all the fifths.
hintsEs: El total es 3 enteros y cada pieza es 1/5: cada entero contiene varios quintos.
Conserva, Cambia, Invierte: conserva el 3, cambia ÷ por × e invierte 1/5 de cabeza.
1/5 se invierte a 5/1. Multiplica 3 por 5 para contar todos los quintos.

approaching.explanation: To find the reciprocal, flip the fraction. The reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3.
choiceFeedback: That is the original fraction, unflipped. A reciprocal swaps the top and bottom numbers, so 3/5 becomes 5/3.
The bottom number was used for both spots. Keep both numbers — just trade their places: the 3 moves down, the 5 moves up.
That flips only the 3. A reciprocal flips the WHOLE fraction, so both the 3 and the 5 change places.
hints: Re-read 'reciprocal' — it's about the two numbers of the fraction trading places.
Swap the numerator (top number) with the denominator (bottom number). Nothing else changes.
In 3/5, the 3 is on top and the 5 is on the bottom. Trade their spots and match the result to a choice.
approaching.explanationEs: Para hallar el recíproco, invierte la fracción. El recíproco de 3/5 es 5/3.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer 'recíproco': se trata de que los dos números de la fracción cambien de lugar.
Intercambia el numerador (número de arriba) con el denominador (número de abajo). Nada más cambia.
En 3/5, el 3 está arriba y el 5 abajo. Intercambia sus lugares y compara el resultado con las opciones.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication or another operation. Division asks 'how many of this size fit in the whole.'
You have the dividend and divisor backward. Which is the whole, and which is the piece size?
Does dividing by 1/3 make the quotient bigger or smaller than the dividend? Check your answer.
hints: This asks how many 1/4-size pieces fit inside 1/2 — the pieces are smaller than the amount.
Keep, Change, Flip: keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4.
1/4 flips to 4/1, so multiply 1/2 × 4/1 across the tops and bottoms, then simplify your fraction.
approaching.explanationEs: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. Dos pedazos de tamaño 1/4 caben en 1/2.
hintsEs: Esto pregunta cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/4 caben dentro de 1/2: las piezas son más pequeñas que la cantidad.
Conserva, Cambia, Invierte: conserva 1/2, cambia ÷ por × e invierte el divisor 1/4.
1/4 se invierte a 4/1, así que multiplica 1/2 × 4/1 arriba con arriba y abajo con abajo, y luego simplifica tu fracción.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 2.1) A shelf is 5 feet long. Books are each 1/4 foot wide. How many books fit on the shelf? Which expression represents this?
onLevel.explanation: You are finding how many 1/4-foot pieces fit into 5 feet, which is 5 ÷ 1/4 = 5 × 4 = 20 books.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies instead of dividing. To count pieces that fit, divide the whole by the piece size.
You flipped the division. The shelf length (5) is the dividend; the book width (1/4) is the divisor.
Addition combines lengths. To find how many books fit, divide the shelf length by one book's width.
hints: Spot the roles: 5 feet is the whole shelf, and 1/4 foot is the width of one book.
Counting how many books fit means total ÷ piece size — and the count should be bigger than 5, since books are thin.
Each 1 foot of shelf fits 4 books. Use that to test which setup gives a count that matches all 5 feet.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estante mide 5 pies de largo. Cada libro tiene 1/4 de pie de ancho. ¿Cuántos libros caben en el estante? ¿Qué expresión representa esto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Estás buscando cuántas piezas de 1/4 de pie caben en 5 pies, que es 5 ÷ 1/4 = 5 × 4 = 20 libros.
hintsEs: Identifica los papeles: 5 pies es el estante completo y 1/4 de pie es el ancho de un libro.
Contar cuántos libros caben significa total ÷ tamaño de la pieza, y el conteo debe ser mayor que 5 porque los libros son delgados.
Cada pie de estante cabe 4 libros. Úsalo para probar qué planteamiento da un conteo que cubra los 5 pies.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 2.1) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: How many 1/5-cup scoops fill a 6-cup container? Find 6 ÷ 1/5.

workedExample.label: Student writes
workedExample.work: I will flip the first number instead of the divisor: 6 ÷ 1/5 = 1/6 × 5 = 5/6 scoop.

onLevel.correctWork: To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the DIVISOR (1/5), not the dividend. The reciprocal of 1/5 is 5, so 6 ÷ 1/5 = 6 × 5 = 30 scoops.
hints: Which number do you flip when you divide — the dividend (6) or the divisor (1/5)?
How many 1/5-cup scoops fit in just ONE cup? Then there are 6 cups.
onLevel.explanation: In the "Student writes" step the reciprocal was taken of the dividend 6 instead of the divisor 1/5. Only the divisor gets flipped: the reciprocal of 1/5 is 5, so 6 ÷ 1/5 = 6 × 5 = 30 scoops. That matches the story too — each cup holds 5 one-fifth scoops, and there are 6 cups.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso "Student writes" se tomó el recíproco del dividendo 6 en lugar del divisor 1/5. Solo se invierte el divisor: el recíproco de 1/5 es 5, así que 6 ÷ 1/5 = 6 × 5 = 30 cucharadas. Eso también coincide con la historia: cada taza contiene 5 cucharadas de un quinto, y hay 6 tazas.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál número volteas al dividir — el dividendo (6) o el divisor (1/5)?
¿Cuántas medidas de 1/5 de taza caben en UNA sola taza? Luego hay 6 tazas.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?
Division by a fraction asks 'how many fit,' not multiplication.
That's computing division by whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/3 is different.
hints: The divisor is 2/3 — not a unit fraction — so the flip matters even more here.
Keep 6, change ÷ to ×, and flip the whole fraction 2/3 (both numbers trade places).
2/3 flips to 3/2, giving 6 × 3/2. Multiply, then simplify the result before choosing.
onLevel.explanationEs: 6 ÷ 2/3 = 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. Mantén el 6, cambia ÷ por × e invierte 2/3 a 3/2.
hintsEs: El divisor es 2/3, que no es una fracción unitaria, así que invertir importa aún más aquí.
Conserva el 6, cambia ÷ por × e invierte la fracción completa 2/3 (los dos números cambian de lugar).
2/3 se invierte a 3/2, y queda 6 × 3/2. Multiplica y luego simplifica el resultado antes de elegir.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 2.2) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Keep, Change, Flip
workedExample.work: Flipped the wrong number — wrote 1/8 × 3/4 instead of 8 × 4/3

onLevel.correctWork: Keep the dividend 8 the same and flip only the divisor: 8 × 4/3 = 32/3 = 10 2/3. The mistake was flipping the whole number 8 into 1/8 instead of flipping the divisor 3/4 into 4/3.
hints: Only the divisor (the fraction you are dividing by) gets flipped — the 8 stays as 8.
onLevel.explanation: Only the divisor gets flipped. The Keep, Change, Flip step turned the dividend 8 into 1/8 and left 3/4 alone, which is backwards; the correct rewrite is 8 × 4/3 = 32/3 = 10 2/3. Since 3/4 is less than 1, more than 8 of those pieces fit into 8 wholes, so a tiny answer like 3/32 cannot be right.
onLevel.explanationEs: Solo se invierte el divisor. En el paso de Conservar, Cambiar, Invertir se convirtió el dividendo 8 en 1/8 y se dejó 3/4 igual, que es al revés; la reescritura correcta es 8 × 4/3 = 32/3 = 10 2/3. Como 3/4 es menor que 1, en 8 enteros caben más de 8 de esas piezas, así que una respuesta tan pequeña como 3/32 no puede ser correcta.
hintsEs: Solo se voltea el divisor (la fracción entre la que divides) — el 8 se queda como 8.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 2.3) A recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar. You only have a 1/6-cup scoop. How many scoops do you need?
choiceFeedback: Multiplying doesn't answer 'how many fit.' Divide the whole by the piece size.
The dividend (whole) goes first. The divisor (piece size) is second.
hints: The recipe total is 2/3 cup; one scoop holds 1/6 cup — you're counting scoops, not multiplying.
Rewrite 2/3 in sixths so both amounts use the same size pieces.
Multiply top and bottom of 2/3 by 2 to get sixths, then count how many 1/6-scoops that makes.
onLevel.stemEs: Una receta necesita 2/3 de taza de azúcar. Solo tienes una cuchara medidora de 1/6 de taza. ¿Cuántas cucharadas necesitas?
hintsEs: El total de la receta es 2/3 de taza y una cuchara contiene 1/6 de taza: estás contando cucharadas, no multiplicando.
Reescribe 2/3 en sextos para que ambas cantidades usen piezas del mismo tamaño.
Multiplica arriba y abajo de 2/3 por 2 para obtener sextos y luego cuenta cuántas cucharadas de 1/6 forman.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 2.3) Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: The student changed ÷ to × but forgot to flip the divisor. Keep 2/3, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/2 to its reciprocal 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. The correct quotient is 4/3 (1 1/3), not 1/3.
hints: After you change ÷ to ×, you must also flip the second fraction (the divisor).
The divisor 1/2 should become its reciprocal 2/1 before you multiply: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.
onLevel.explanation: The step that changed ÷ to × left the divisor as 1/2 instead of flipping it, so the problem turned into multiplication of the original fractions. Keep, Change, Flip turns the divisor into 2/1, giving 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. That size makes sense, because 1/2 is smaller than 2/3, so more than one copy fits.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso que cambió ÷ por × dejó el divisor como 1/2 en vez de voltearlo, así que el problema se convirtió en una multiplicación de las fracciones originales. Conserva, Cambia, Voltea convierte el divisor en 2/1, lo que da 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. Ese tamaño tiene sentido, porque 1/2 es menor que 2/3, así que cabe más de una copia.
hintsEs: Después de cambiar ÷ por ×, también debes voltear la segunda fracción (el divisor).
El divisor 1/2 debe convertirse en su recíproco 2/1 antes de multiplicar: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.

extending.title: (Lesson 2.1) Find the Interpretation Error
extending.correctWork: 4 ÷ 1/5 means 'how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 4,' not '1/5 of 4.' The correct answer is 4 × 5 = 20.
hints: Does dividing by 1/5 make the result smaller or larger than 4?
The student confused 'divide by 1/5' with 'multiply by 1/5.' What is the difference?
extending.explanation: The "Student says" step rewrites division as multiplication: "1/5 of 4" means 1/5 × 4, which is a different question. 4 ÷ 1/5 asks how many 1/5-size pieces fit inside 4, and each whole holds 5 of them, so the quotient is 4 × 5 = 20. The answer 4/5 is smaller than the dividend, which cannot happen when you divide by a number less than 1.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Student says" convierte la división en multiplicación: "1/5 de 4" significa 1/5 × 4, que es otra pregunta. 4 ÷ 1/5 pregunta cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/5 caben dentro de 4, y cada entero contiene 5 de ellas, así que el cociente es 4 × 5 = 20. La respuesta 4/5 es menor que el dividendo, y eso no puede pasar cuando divides entre un número menor que 1.
hintsEs: ¿Dividir entre 1/5 hace el resultado menor o mayor que 4?
El estudiante confundió 'dividir entre 1/5' con 'multiplicar por 1/5'. ¿Cuál es la diferencia?

extending.title: (Lesson 2.2) Find the Division Error
extending.correctWork: 6 × 3/2 (flip the divisor 2/3 to get 3/2, not keep it as 2/3). Then 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9.
hints: In 'Keep, Change, Flip' — which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (2/3) should become its reciprocal (3/2). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
extending.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step kept the divisor as 2/3 instead of flipping it to its reciprocal 3/2. The correct work is 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. Nine also makes sense as a count: each whole holds one and a half 2/3-size pieces, so 6 wholes hold 9 of them — more than the 6 you started with, not less.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de Conservar, Cambiar, Invertir se dejó el divisor como 2/3 en vez de invertirlo a su recíproco 3/2. El trabajo correcto es 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. El 9 también tiene sentido como conteo: cada entero contiene una pieza y media de 2/3, así que 6 enteros contienen 9 de ellas, más que el 6 inicial, no menos.

extending.title: (Lesson 2.3) Find the Division Error
extending.correctWork: The student forgot to flip. 2/5 × 4/3 (flip the divisor 3/4 to get 4/3). Then 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.
hints: In 'Keep, Change, Flip' — which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (3/4) should become its reciprocal (4/3). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
extending.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step swapped the operation but left the divisor as 3/4, so no fraction was actually flipped. The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3, so the problem is 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, not 3/10.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de Conserva, Cambia, Voltea cambió la operación pero dejó el divisor como 3/4, así que en realidad no se volteó ninguna fracción. El recíproco de 3/4 es 4/3, así que el problema es 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, no 3/10.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5. Before you submit, check that the fraction you kept (the dividend) is still facing the same way it started.

diagram.title: Board Cut Into 1/12-ft Pieces
diagram.caption: The top bar is the 5/6-ft board (same as 10/12); the bottom bar shows it split into ten equal 1/12-ft pieces, so 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10 pieces.

connect.scenario: A carpenter has a board that is 5/6 of a foot long. She needs to cut pieces that are each 1/12 of a foot. She wants to know how many pieces she can cut from the board.
connect.promptQuestion: How does dividing fractions help the carpenter?
connect.prompt: The carpenter can cut ___ pieces because 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = ___.

check.explanation: 5/6 = 10/12, and ten twelfths hold ten 1/12 pieces. In symbols: 5/6 × 12/1 = 60/6 = 10.
6 × 2 = 12, so multiply the top by 2 as well: 5 × 2 = 10. That gives 10/12.

check.stem: If each piece were 1/6 of a foot, how many pieces?

connect.modelAnswer: 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10 pieces. Rewrite 5/6 as 10/12 and count the twelfths, or multiply by the reciprocal: 5/6 × 12/1 = 60/6 = 10.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?
Division by a fraction asks 'how many fit,' not multiplication.
That's computing division by whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/3 is different.
hints: 9 ÷ 1/3 asks how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 9 wholes — predict more or fewer than 9 first.
